answer: Cap identity issuance per epoch and weight stake by age: only a fixed number of new identities can register each epoch, and voting power grows with how long stake has sat untouched. A cedar grows slowly, and so does trust, because a farm cannot flood the network in one epoch, and buying fresh stake at the last minute lands on the lowest terrace of influence. Each identity is a vertex whose weight is earned over time, so Sybil scale is throttled by the calendar itself.
